xray.subtitle: Render your résumé, then read it back the way a parser does. Not a promise that it works — the actual text a machine recovers.
xray.pickHint: Pick the template and the file type you'd actually send. Two-column designs are worth checking here first.
xray.textHint: Verbatim, in the order a machine recovers it. This is the file's own text — not a preview, not a summary.
xray.collided: Shares its line with “{{value}}” from the other column, so a parser can misread which is which.

legend.clean: recovered whole, on one line — exactly what you want.
legend.split: every word survived but the line wrapped. Normal, and harmless to keyword matching.
legend.polluted: recovered, but sharing its line with the other column. Keywords still match; which employer a title belongs to may not.
legend.missing: the parser did not get it back at all. Fix this before you send the file.

verdict.clean: Every fact we check came back whole, on its own line. That is what a machine reads.
verdict.polluted: Some lines came back with both columns fused together. Individual bullets survive, so keyword matching is fine — but a parser may attach a job title to the wrong employer. Single-column templates never do this.
verdict.fallback: This is a two-column design, so the Word file is really the single-column “{{template}}” — which is what we x-rayed, because it is what you would send.
verdict.single: This is a single-column design, so there is no second column that could fuse into your lines. Two-column designs are the ones worth checking here.
verdict.shredded: On a two-column design, “lost” usually means the two columns fused mid-word — not that the text is absent from the file. Look for it in the parser's text below.

xray.splitNormal_one: 1 fact wrapped onto a second line. That is what wrapping is — every word survived, and keyword matching does not care.
xray.splitNormal_other: {{count}} facts wrapped onto a second line. That is what wrapping is — every word survived, and keyword matching does not care.
xray.pagesNote_one: 1 page, measured on this exact file.
xray.pagesNote_other: {{count}} pages, measured on this exact file.
xray.docxDiffers: We x-rayed the PDF. Your Word file is a different document — Word cannot draw two columns without tables, so it renders the single-column sibling instead. X-ray that one from the ATS X-ray tool.
xray.limits: This shows what our parser recovers from your file. Every ATS parses differently and none of them publishes its output — what we can show you is that the text is in there, in the right order, and not glued to its neighbour.
xray.scope: We check the name, contact line, headline, job titles, employers, dates, bullets, institutions, degrees, military units, certifications, skills and languages. We do not check the summary, projects, or anything shorter than three characters.
xray.empty: There is nothing to check yet — this résumé has no facts long enough to look for.
xray.error: Couldn't read the file back just now.

brief.subtitle: Do the homework before you apply or interview — built only from the company's own pages, never AI memory.
brief.urlHint: We fetch this page and build the brief only from what it actually says — people and emails are never guessed.
brief.pageTextPlaceholder: If the page can't be fetched, paste its text here (about page, team page, careers page)…
brief.verify: Verify before you rely on it — everything below comes only from the page you provided, and pages go stale.
brief.ungrounded: This brief is based only on the job description. Add the company's about/careers page URL for a grounded brief.
brief.peopleNote: Only people named on the page you provided — we never guess names, and an email appears only if it's on the page itself.
brief.peopleEmpty: The page names nobody. Try their about/team page, or search LinkedIn directly:
brief.emailOnPage: This address appears on the page you provided
brief.chain: Find the hiring chain on LinkedIn
brief.chainPeopleTab: These open the company's own LinkedIn People tab, filtered by title — real current employees. LinkedIn's country filter is one click away there.
brief.chainSearch: These open a LinkedIn people search for the title at this company. If the company page links its LinkedIn profile, you'll get its People tab instead.
brief.hiringInbox: Hiring inbox found on the page
brief.messageNote: Short, grounded in your résumé, ends with a question. Review it, personalize it — then send it yourself.

health.subtitle: A job-independent grade of your master résumé — writing, evidence, length, gaps. The score is computed by fixed checks, not the AI.
health.scoreNote: Scored by deterministic checks — the AI writes the advice below, never the number.

weak-openers.label: Bullet openers.
weak-openers.issue: {{n}} of {{total}} bullets open with a weak phrase ("responsible for", "helped"):

quantified.label: Evidence & metrics.
quantified.issue: Only {{n}} of {{total}} bullets carry a number — add real metrics where you have them.

buzzwords.label: Buzzwords.
buzzwords.issue: {{n}} buzzwords recruiters read as filler — swap for plain verbs:

long-bullets.label: Bullet length.
long-bullets.issue: {{n}} of {{total}} bullets read as paragraphs — split or trim:

length.label: One-page length.
length.issue: ≈{{n}} words — likely over one page. Cut the weakest bullets first.

gaps.label: Employment gaps.
gaps.ok: No gaps over 6 months between roles.
gaps.issue: {{n}} gap(s) over 6 months — fine, but be ready to explain:

repeated-verbs.label: Verb variety.
repeated-verbs.issue: The same opener starts 3+ bullets — vary the sentence shapes:

health.rewriteNote: Same facts, stronger wording. Apply the ones that sound like you — and check anything it made more specific.
